items.title: Meta's $1M Global AI Developer Hackathon
points: Meta is hosting a $1M Global AI Developer Hackathon running October 26–November 4, 2026, held virtually worldwide
$150 in free Meta Model API credits given per participant to offset development costs
Two competition tracks: Indie Developer and Startup; applications close October 25

Developers get access to Meta's newest AI models: Llama, Muse Image (image generation), SAM 3.1 (Segment Anything Model 3.1, a computer vision model that identifies and isolates objects in images), and the Muse Code agent (automated code generation assistant)
Open-weights models (AI models released publicly so developers can download and run them locally) are available to use
Live workshops led by Meta team members and partner organizations focus on real-world problem-solving and identifying user pain points

issues.subject: ☕️ Build with Meta’s newest AI models at their $1M Hackathon

headlines: Meta is hosting a $1M Global AI Developer Hackathon from October 26–November 4 with $150 in free API credits per participant
Developers can build with Meta's newest AI models including Llama, Muse Image, SAM 3.1, and the Muse Code agent
Hackathon is virtual and worldwide with two competition tracks: Indie Developer and Startup
Applications close October 25 and winners receive cash prizes from a $1M prize pool

sections.title: Hackathon Overview & Prize Structure
points: 10-day hackathon running October 26–November 4, 2026 with virtual and worldwide participation
$1 million in total cash prizes distributed among winning projects
$150 per participant in Meta Model API credits to offset development costs
Two competition tracks available: Indie Developer track and Startup track

sections.title: Available Tools & Technologies
points: Access to Meta's latest generative AI models via the Meta Model API
Muse Image for image generation tasks
SAM 3.1 (Segment Anything Model 3.1—a computer vision model for identifying and isolating objects in images)
Muse Code agent for automated code generation and assistance
Open-weights models (AI models released publicly so developers can download and run them locally)

sections.title: Learning & Support
points: Live workshops delivered by Meta team members and partner organizations
Focus on real-world problem-solving: participants guided to identify target users and their pain points
Platform encourages experimentation with AI capabilities to explore new possibilities
